title: A law grows a network that reads its own distance plainly at every stage, but only a line
subject: Networks of rings joined by shared contacts, read with the canonical knot test on their space-time law
conclusion: Inserting one ring at a time into the twist torus of rings, a local rewiring of the three contacts spanning the gap, grows a network whose every stage keeps every contact persistent and reads its distance across time without freezing. Through tori of the regular lattices no growth can do this in two dimensions: an on-time torus of large index is a tube, with balls growing linearly.
